requirements.description: The system shall allow a new shipment to be registered by providing its origin, destination, and delivery deadline.
Each registered shipment shall receive a unique tracking identifier.
The shipment origin and destination shall be different.
The shipment origin shall remain fixed throughout the logistics lifecycle.
Shipment registration may be completed even before a route is defined.
The delivery deadline shall be mandatory and shall serve as a criterion for trip planning.
The system shall allow the origin and destination to be selected only from previously registered logistics locations.
The system shall query and present candidate routes compatible with the shipment's needs.
A candidate route shall be considered valid only when it satisfies the shipment's origin, final destination, and delivery deadline.
The user shall be able to choose one of the presented routes and associate it with the shipment.
When a shipment does not yet have a defined route, it shall be identified as "unrouted".
When no route meets the specified criteria, the system shall inform the user that no feasible option exists for the current specification.
The system shall display the legs of the selected route, including loading and unloading points, trips, and planned dates.
The system shall allow the destination of an existing shipment to be changed.
The new destination shall be neither the shipment's origin nor its current destination.
When the destination is changed, the system shall reassess the shipment's current route.
When the current route no longer serves the new destination, the shipment shall require a new routing decision.
The system shall allow routes to be replanned for shipments that have deviated from the planned route or whose destination has changed.
The system shall allow a shipment to be looked up by its tracking identifier.
When a shipment is looked up, the system shall present its current status.
The system shall provide the shipment's last known location.
The system shall provide the estimated arrival time when the shipment has a valid route and is progressing in accordance with the plan.
The system shall retain and display the history of logistics events associated with the shipment.
The history shall distinguish expected events from events that occurred outside the plan.
The system shall flag when a shipment has deviated from its expected route.
The system shall allow the shipment to be viewed with geographic support, highlighting its origin, final destination, and last known location.
The system shall provide a consolidated administrative view of shipments.
Shipments shall be grouped, at a minimum, into the categories "unrouted", "routed and in transit", and "collected by the recipient".
The system shall allow the details of any shipment to be opened from the administrative view.
Routed shipments that have not yet been collected shall be trackable as shipments in transit.
The system shall allow logistics events of the following types to be recorded: receipt, loading, unloading, customs clearance, and pickup.
Every logistics event shall be associated with an existing shipment.
Every logistics event shall specify the location where it occurred and the date of occurrence.
Loading and unloading events shall be associated with the corresponding trip.
Events other than loading or unloading shall not require a trip identifier.
The system shall reject attempts to record an event with a non-existent shipment, location, or trip.
Recording a valid event shall update the shipment's operational status.
After each valid event, the system shall recalculate information such as transport status, known location, expected next step, and adherence to the plan.
When an event indicates execution that differs from the planned route, the shipment shall be marked as off route.
When a shipment is unloaded at its final destination, the system shall mark it as having arrived at the destination.
When pickup by the recipient is recorded, the shipment shall be considered complete from a logistics perspective.
The system shall allow logistics events to be recorded through more than one operational channel.
The supported channels shall include, at a minimum, an operational interface, an integration service, and input-file processing.
The system shall provide a consolidated view of shipments for use by monitoring channels.
The system shall keep monitoring channels aligned with the most recent status of each shipment.
The system shall preserve consistency among shipment registration, the planned route, and completed events.
No invalid event may alter the shipment's state.
Rules concerning origin, destination, deadline, and route compatibility shall be applied uniformly across all operational channels.
The shipment's status shall be recalculated whenever there is a relevant change in planning or execution.
The system shall maintain sufficient history to reconstruct the shipment's logistics lifecycle.
Each event shall retain, at a minimum, the time at which it occurred and the time at which it was recorded in the system.
Rejected recording attempts shall be identifiable for subsequent operational analysis.
The system shall allow correctly delivered shipments, shipments still in transit, and shipments with operational deviations to be distinguished.
Shipment status updates shall occur in time to support operational monitoring.
Event intake shall continue even when detailed status recalculation occurs in the background.
Inputs received through files shall be processed periodically without requiring constant manual triggering.
Monitoring channels shall reflect the most recent available information about the shipment.
Information presented to users shall be organized by business status rather than solely by technical structure.
Operational navigation shall facilitate frequent tasks such as locating a shipment, viewing details, selecting a route, and recording an event.
The system shall reduce operational errors through controlled lists of locations, trips, event types, and shipment identifiers.
Error messages and no-route messages shall be understandable for administrative and logistics use.
A failure in an isolated recording attempt shall not compromise the processing of other shipments.
Records received in an invalid format shall be separated for later handling without interrupting the remainder of the workload.
The system shall treat off-route shipments as visible operational exceptions to enable prompt corrective action.
The system shall maintain consistency among the data shown in the administrative interface, tracking, mobile channels, and integrations.
The shipment's primary information shall be exchangeable in standardized formats to facilitate integration with other systems.
The tracking model shall be unique regardless of the channel used to record or look up the shipment.
